meta.face: Three clearly different men of Asia Minor with olive skin of different warmth. TARACHUS (centre), about sixty-five, a veteran: a BROAD, SQUARE, heavy-boned face with a FLAT, wide forehead, a BROKEN, slightly crooked nose with a flattened bridge, small, deep-set, steady grey eyes under thick, straight, grizzled brows, a wide, set mouth, a strong, square chin; close-cropped iron-grey hair and a short, dense, square-cut grey beard. PROBUS (left), about forty, a plebeian of Side: a LONG, LEAN face with its length in the lower half — a LONG upper lip, HOLLOW cheeks, a long, thin nose with a slight hook, large, dark, earnest eyes set CLOSE together under thin, arched black brows, a narrow, ROUNDED chin; short, untidy black hair and a thin, sparse black beard along the jaw. ANDRONICUS (right), about twenty-two, a patrician of Ephesus: BEARDLESS, with a smooth, BROAD-CHEEKED, softly HEXAGONAL face — wide, flat cheekbones, a short, straight Greek nose continuing the line of the brow, large, wide-set, light-brown eyes, a full, well-cut mouth, a firm chin; short, neat, wavy chestnut hair. Not the young, clean-shaven, triangular-faced companion of theban_legion, the brothers of nereus_achilleus or faustinus_jovita, or the two young Palestinians of adrian_eubulus.
meta.basis: No likenesses survive; the ages and ranks are those of the first version of their Acts as summarised by Wikipedia (Tarachus a former soldier of about sixty-five, Probus a plebeian of Side, Andronicus a patrician of Ephesus), and the peaceful beasts are the book's. The Greek fresco on Wikipedia shows them as a greybeard, a bearded man and a youth.
